children.author: mgantlett
children.text:
Single RTX 4080 (16GB VRAM) on a NixOS Linux workstation running llama.cpp (llama-server on CUDA 12.9).

The biggest unlock on 16GB cards lately has been MoE models plus quantized KV caches. Right now my daily driver is gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (UD-Q4_K_M GGUF, so you get 26B knowledge capacity at 4B active-parameter speed) running alongside a small dedicated llama-server embedding process on the same GPU.

With -fa on (flash attention) and -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 KV-cache quantization, I can keep a 32k context window (-c 32768 -np 2 parallel slots, -ngl 23 when the F16 mmproj vision projector is loaded, -ngl 26 text-only) comfortable without OOMing. For denser single-slot coding runs I swap to Qwen3.8-27B-IQ3_M with the same q4_0 KV cache flags.

Zero desire to build a multi-GPU space heater at home yet - q4_0 KV cache + 26B-A4B MoE stretched what a single 16GB card can usefully do way further than I expected a year ago.

children.author: selicos
children.text:
I bought a Framework Desktop mainboard only, 128gb AMD 395+ setup, and put it in an existing case with PSU i had on hand. I had a fan for it. It was $2699 +$15 expedited shipping. The case and PSU/etc was probably $200 more (It's an overkill 850w SFX PSU and cheap but great ITX case from Deepcool).

I started with Ubuntu but pivoted to Fedora over the summer after a recommendation from a security engineer friend. And it is mostly easier.

Generic setup doc here: (not fully updated with GUFO): https://github.com/Selicos/AI_Tools_Public/blob/main/docs/Fe...

Key changes for other distros are how to load drivers/apps and get running. Ubuntu has a recent CVE issue but worked fine. CachyOS/etc set up for more Windows like UI and transplants was fine but not focused on the Stricx Halo setup. Although I do see close to RTX 5070 performance in most games I've tested.

I was running LM Studio and some other runtimes for ease of setup and model switching. Once you settle on a runtime and model setup you like it is easy to set it up, let it run, and manage as needed.

Last week I set up GUFO, as it targets the AMD Strix Halo hardware and is efficient for Qwen Flash Next. I could probably get the work done with Qwen 3.8 27B but I like how QFN thinks and lets me follow along. Starting at about 260k context, I see 88gb of RAM usage when loaded and about 108gb when in use, depending on context overhead. I do have to restart the model every so often as Copilot Chat in VS Code starts failing.

I have also run Lemonade, llama.cpp directly, vllm, and more. Custom or bespoke runtimes for your hardware are key, like Srata or GUFO. I need to look at llama-swap. LM Studio is easy and with their Tailscale backed link feature you can stay connected from any device.

IF it supports OpenAI/etc back end you're mostly there. Get the model running and connect from your preferred harness/etc. GUFO works well with Copilot Chat in VS Code. I need to connect it to Pi and openhands/etc later this week once I get this test project in a good spot.

Qwen 3.8 27B, Gemma 4 26B A4B variants, whisper, and more run well. A Spark or bank of GPUs would do better, of course, but not for under $3k for 128gb of memory. I have tested adding an Nvidia 3060 12gb to the Strix Halo but the iGPU is turned off by Fedora and I didn't have more time to solve.

My secondary Fedora AI system has the 3060 12gb and a 5900XT (16c/32t) plus 64gb of DDR4-3200. I need to get Strata up on it and see how well medium sized models work on the mixed memory. I bet MOE models will work well. I have the hardware so will use it but renting capacity is much cheaper if you just want to mess around and get used to the tools.

Happy to answer questions about how I got here. I'm an infra guy, not a software dev, and what I'm doing with AI at home could definitely be 5x faster with a real dev and dev process.

Cool setup

my 'local llm on a budget' has cost me just about $2,400 in total, spread over a bout 3 years of accumulating stuff.

I got my first 7900xt 20gb on a good sale shortly after they came out in an open box deal on ebay for $590.

After another 7900xt 20gb popped up on facebook marketplace recently for $420, I sniped that and then got a microcenter deal on an asus proart board, 32gb of ddr5, and a 9950x for $1050.

A couple more deals for used cases, an older 1tb nvme ssd I had lying around, and a nice PSU finished the build.

I run Qwen 3.8 27b on linux and have tuned the llama.ccp / rocm setup substantially with the help of codex and claude. I get ~80-110 tok/s depending on all kinds of factors and full 256k context windows with a 6-bit quant.

It's surprisingly capable and I love that I can run it indefinitely, tuning as it goes to behave more like a frontier model.

text: Figured I'd ask here because I have no doubt some of you are running some pretty cool, cost effective solutions for local models. Don't doubt some have mini data centers in their closets either haha, but just looking to get a view into what fellow HN'ers are using for their day to day work.
